newsitem.title: UK: UK budget deficit 5.8 percent of GDP in 1995.
newsitem.headline: UK budget deficit 5.8 percent of GDP in 1995.

text.p: Britain had a general government financial deficit, calculated under the European Union's system of integrated accounts, of 5.8 percent of gross domestic product in calendar 1995, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said.
This compared with 6.8 percent in calendar 1994.
General government gross debt at the end of calendar 1995 (nominal value) was 54.1 percent of GDP compared with 50.4 percent at the end of 1994.
Under the Maastricht Treaty, countries wishing to join a single currency should have deficits not exceeding three percent of GDP and debt not exceeding 60 percent.
Britain's own national accounts are based on a financial year ending April 5.
The ONS estimated the general government financial deficit for the 1995/96 financial year at 5.1 percent of GDP and general government gross debt at 53.8 percent of GDP.
